title: Bitcoin Remains Stuck Near $64,000 as AI Compute Boom Draws Capital Away
excerpt: The largest cryptocurrency has traded in a narrow range for months as massive AI infrastructure spending keeps inflation elevated, rates high, and investor capital flowing elsewhere.
body:
• Bitcoin has traded in a narrow $58,000–$67,000 range for over two months, with the price near $64,200 on Monday, as the AI infrastructure boom absorbs capital that might otherwise flow into crypto.
  • The Federal Reserve has linked recent inflation pressure directly to AI investment, with hyperscalers committing nearly $400 billion in combined 2026 capital spending on data centers, chips and energy infrastructure.
  • Bitcoin miners are increasingly pivoting to AI compute — Hut 8 signed a $9.8 billion AI data center lease and Riot struck a deal with Anthropic — blurring the line between crypto and AI infrastructure.

Bitcoin traded near $64,200 on Monday, up about 1% on the day but still locked inside the $58,000–$67,000 channel it has occupied since late May. The world's largest cryptocurrency has failed to mount a sustained rally despite six consecutive days of spot ETF inflows, as a parallel investment boom in artificial intelligence continues to drain capital, stoke inflation and keep interest rates elevated.

The AI Inflation Loop

The Federal Reserve directly linked part of the recent inflation pressure to AI investment in its June meeting minutes, citing strong demand for data centers, electricity and high-tech equipment as price drivers. Officials warned that AI spending could keep economic growth above its sustainable rate, making inflation more persistent.

The corporate numbers underscore the scale. Alphabet raised its 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $195 billion–$205 billion after Google Cloud revenue jumped 82%. Microsoft expects to spend roughly $190 billion this year. Nvidia reported data-center revenue up 92% year-on-year to $75.2 billion in its latest quarter.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh noted that high-tech equipment investment had grown by nearly 25% year-on-year. U.S. consumer prices remain 3.5% above year-ago levels, and producer prices are up 5.5% — both well above the thresholds that would give the Fed room to ease policy.

Higher Rates, Stronger Dollar, Less Room for Bitcoin

The two-year Treasury yield reached 4.301% last week, its highest in over a year. The 10-year yield approached 4.66%. Higher yields make government bonds and cash more attractive relative to volatile assets like Bitcoin.

"For now, an expensive dollar and high bond yields are pulling liquidity away from risky assets such as cryptocurrencies."

— Nikita Zuborev, senior analyst, BestChange

The dollar index, bolstered by rate expectations and renewed Middle East tensions, sat near 99.4 — another headwind for Bitcoin, which tends to weaken when the dollar strengthens. Semiconductor stocks, meanwhile, have returned roughly 69% in 2026, while Bitcoin remains down about 25% for the year.

Miners Pivot to AI

The convergence of crypto and AI infrastructure continued to accelerate. Hut 8, a Bitcoin miner expanding into AI, saw its shares surge after signing a $9.8 billion, 15-year lease to build 352 MW of AI computing capacity at its Texas campus using Nvidia's data center design. The deal brought the total contracted value at its Beacon Point campus to $19.6 billion.

Riot Platforms struck a deal with AI developer Anthropic, temporarily lifting its stock by 20% before gains faded. Other miners including Cipher Mining and TeraWulf also rose on the trend.

What Would Break the Range

Spot ETFs recorded $203.2 million in net inflows last Tuesday, but the total remains modest against $6.9 billion in outflows during May and June. Analysts say Bitcoin would need lower inflation, falling bond yields, a less hawkish Fed and sustained institutional demand to break convincingly above $67,000.

The Fed's next rate decision looms as the near-term catalyst. Until then, Bitcoin remains caught between improving flow dynamics and an AI investment cycle that shows no signs of cooling — keeping money expensive and risk appetite constrained.
nri_angle: The AI-driven inflation pressure affecting Bitcoin also shapes the broader macro environment for Indian investors with exposure to both crypto and tech equities.
